method: NFL records use nflverse regular-season closing spreads from 2002 through week 9 of 2026. College records use ESPN schedules and closing spreads from 2012 through week 4 of 2026. Week 10 college results are on the previous board against the number posted Nov 5, and they are not inside the record. The search covers home and road, favorite and dog, spread size, division and conference, rest, surface, weather, primetime, the total, and the previous game: margin, points, cover, and streak. It graded 259,428 NFL and 36,602 college combinations that had a full sample. A situation is badged only when it hit at least 60% overall, at least 57% both before 2019 and since, and the lower edge of the rate still beats 52%. The same bar is applied in reverse against the spread and the total. Straight-up fades are not kept: a dog losing the game is the favorite's win, not a finding. If the side that fits is 7–43 against the number, the other side of those games is 43–7 and is badged the same way, with the same cap, and both records are kept. The library also keeps the next tier, in both directions: at least 55.5% overall, at least 53% on both sides of 2019, with a large sample whose lower edge still beats 51%. Near-duplicates were removed. A fade that is the same bet as a cover already kept is dropped. NFL moneylines are graded at the closing American price, one unit risked. A moneyline is badged when that price was profitable before 2019 and since, at least 2% in each era and 5% overall, and the lower edge of the return is still above zero. Winning the game is not enough, and a favorite's win rate is not a system. College has no archived moneyline, so those stay games won. Totals are wins against the closing number. Where the NFL archive has the over and under price, the card also shows the profit at that juice. Hit rate is wins divided by wins plus losses. Pushes are listed and left out. On a fade, the cover record is the other side. The criteria record is that result flipped, which matches the side that fit. The upcoming slate is not inside the historical record. NFL week 10 lines are the nflverse posted number on Nov 14. College week 11 lines are the ESPN posted number (DraftKings) on Nov 14. Neither is a closing line, and both can move. Each game also lists up to three matchup splits: the series, the same weekday or venue role, that week of the season, primetime, and weather or a dome when the archive knows the conditions. The series is shown at 70% or better. A team's own day, week, or building split is shown at 75%, and anything under 8 games has to be 75% either way. A day that is most of a team's schedule is left off. These notes are this series or this team before the kickoff. They are not a league-wide system.
